note: plan.md section 7.2 -- the sixteen critical negative tests -- expressed as an executable specification. Each entry either POINTS AT the suite that already proves it (nothing is duplicated and nothing is weakened; referencing an existing suite is the correct disposition) or is explicitly STAGED with the module and phase that will own it. A staged entry is a visible debt with a name, not a silent gap: the security gate fails if an entry has neither an owner nor a phase, and fails if a referenced suite does not exist in tests/contracts/expected-suites.json.

enforcedBy.test: a user with no project membership cannot be scoped to any project
a membership-less user's tenant-wide read still excludes other tenants
a row read outside the scope is denied, and no-membership means no row

specs.note: Phase 4 found the real bug here: `in ()` for an empty project list is a PostgreSQL parse error, so the most-protected request 500s. CrmQueryScopeTest pins the `and 1 = 0` SQL.

specs.requirement: project ID from another tenant cannot be used for read or write

enforcedBy.test: a tenant B project id in an A request is denied before any query runs
a cross-project read is denied for an EMPLOYEE and permitted for an ADMIN
a cross-project write is denied and the target row is unchanged
tenant A never sees tenant B's rows, and the SQL carries the predicate

specs.requirement: unauthorized aggregates do not reveal counts or sums

enforcedBy.test: counts and distinct counts are scoped, so an aggregate never includes an unauthorized row
an aggregate restricted to one project cannot be widened by a client filter

specs.requirement: unauthorized rows/fields do not appear in CSV or DOCX
specs.stagedBecause: no export module exists. plan.md section 6 requires authorization BEFORE aggregation, which is a different assertion from 'the response was filtered'.
no export module exists; a signed URL without a reauthorization at download is the defect this test exists to catch

specs.requirement: human takeover aborts an in-flight AI send

enforcedBy.test: a worker that dies after the provider send does not send the reply twice

specs.note: The mode/modeVersion transition and the conditional outbound send are the same assertion; Phase 4's journey walks it, Phase 5b's crash test pins the send half. A dedicated concurrency test (a takeover racing an in-flight send in the same transaction window) is still owed in Phase 6 -- recorded in docs/migration/phases/phase-06.md ownership, not here.

specs.requirement: duplicated webhooks create one message and one usage event

enforcedBy.test: one webhook admits one event; the redelivery is refused and nothing is republished
five redeliveries still produce exactly one message and one intent
the database itself refuses a second row for the same provider message id
the same provider id in another tenant is a different event

specs.note: The USAGE EVENT half is not implemented: the usage ledger is Phase 8. The uniqueness half is enforced today, and a duplicate that produced two usage events would be a Phase-8 regression to add.

specs.requirement: worker crash after external send does not duplicate on retry

enforcedBy.test: a worker that dies after the provider send does not send the reply twice
an expired lease is reclaimed and the re-run still does not duplicate the send
a retried job does not send the same reply twice
a worker that does not hold the lease cannot complete, retry or dead-letter

specs.requirement: outbox dispatch after commit does not publish rolled-back changes

enforcedBy.test: a rolled-back reply publishes nothing: the intent shares the transaction's fate
a committed reply inside an outer transaction is durable
a rolled-back domain transaction publishes nothing
publishing outside a transaction is refused, and nothing is written
a replay records who, when, and what it replays, and mutates no history
a second replay of the same event writes nothing and is still audited
a machine principal cannot replay: an unattributable replay is refused
replay is audited, idempotent, and never creates a second row
